The proposed polarization conversion metasurface (PCM) consists of a double-headed arrow unit cell and its 90°, 180°, and 270° rotated versions.
The PCM demonstrates an ultra-wide 10-dB RCS reduction bandwidth from 9 to 40 GHz, corresponding to a fractional bandwidth of 126.5%.
The PCM is implemented on a thin, low-cost FR-4 substrate with an air gap, resulting in a lightweight and low-profile design.
The 10-dB RCS reduction bandwidth is more than 63% for TE polarization and more than 32% for TM polarization up to 50-degree incident angles.

The double-headed arrow unit cell supports multiple plasmon resonances that are excited by electric field components along the unit cell's anisotropic axes, enabling efficient polarization conversion.
The 180-degree phase difference between the PCM unit cell and its mirror creates destructive interference and RCS reduction.
The fabricated 3x3 array of the proposed PCM tiles demonstrates good agreement between simulation and measurement results.
Compared to previous works, the proposed metasurface has significantly higher RCS reduction bandwidth, with 126.5% for normal incidence.
The low-profile, low-cost, and lightweight characteristics of the proposed metasurface make it suitable for practical applications in stealth platforms.

The 3D scattered radiation patterns of the proposed metasurface show that the incident wave is redirected into four main lobes at diagonal planes instead of a single main lobe reflected from a PEC surface.
The RCS reduction of the proposed metasurface is more than 42.81 dB and 19 dB in the principal and diagonal planes, respectively, at 9.75 GHz.
The RCS reduction of the proposed metasurface is more than 35 dB and 29 dB in the principal and diagonal planes, respectively, at 14.35 GHz.
The proposed metasurface is implemented on a commercially available FR-4 substrate with a thickness of 0.25 mm, making it a low-cost and lightweight solution.
The air gap between the FR-4 substrate and the ground plane contributes to the low-profile and lightweight design of the proposed metasurface.
The fabricated PCM surface with an overall size of 200 mm × 200 mm is composed of a 3x3 array of the proposed unit cell tiles.
